items.reason: The hooks are no longer a setup step: every everyday justfile recipe (check, build, test, lint, fmt, fmt-check, run, dev, ci) now depends on a private `_hooks-auto` that points core.hooksPath at .githooks/ the first time any `just` command runs in a clone — writing only an UNSET value so an explicit `just hooks-uninstall` or a custom path is never overridden, never failing a recipe, and opt-out-able with PUMPER_NO_HOOKS=1 — and the one rung that a per-clone hook can never guarantee (commit-message shape) was additionally made server-side: `scripts/ci/commit-lint.mjs` is now the single implementation, `.githooks/commit-msg` delegates to it, and the `Conventional commits` step in the `Ship inventory` CI job judges every commit in `origin/<base>..HEAD` on each pull request, so an uninstalled hook or a `--no-verify` no longer skips the rule. `scripts/ci/commit-lint.test.mjs` (wired into `just inventory`, `just ci` and the CI job) proves the gate can go red on eight unconventional subjects, pins the 0/2/3 exit-code contract, and reconciles the wiring itself: the hook must delegate, its sh fallback type list must equal the shared TYPES, the listed recipes must still carry `_hooks-auto`, and ci.yml must still run the gate. Honest limits: git cannot install hooks at clone time, so a contributor who only ever runs bare cargo still has none locally (which is exactly why the commit rule also runs in CI); and the scan's question about how many past CI failures a default hook would have caught could not be answered here — reading CI history needs network.

lessons: A local guardrail in this org's repos should ship in two halves, and the report should say which half is which: the local half (auto-installed git hooks, for fast feedback before the commit exists) and a server-side rung running the SAME file (for the clone that never opted in, and for `--no-verify`). Shipping only the local half is what makes an opt-in hook read as enforcement while refusing nothing.

In pumper, a rule stated in two places will be tested for agreement or it will drift: the repo's own idiom is the EXPECTED-diff inventory test (crates/server/src/routes/mod.rs), and it applies to non-Rust surfaces too — the commit-msg hook's sh fallback types are now reconciled against the JS list, and the justfile recipes are asserted to still carry the auto-install prerequisite.

Adding a CI job to this repo is not free of gates: `.github/unpinned-actions.json` carries a `ceiling` that counts `uses:` REFERENCES and only ever moves down, so a new job with its own checkout/setup-node would turn `just pin-check` red. Extend an existing job instead, or pin the new references to SHAs (which needs network).

This session had no shell, so nothing here was executed — the node suites and the workflow change are reviewed-correct, not observed-green. When an Ascent lane cannot run a check it adds, say so rather than implying a passing run; the repo's own doctrine is that a cannot-check is not a pass.
